newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Lee urges Taiwanese to work hard in Year of Ox.
newsitem.headline: Lee urges Taiwanese to work hard in Year of Ox.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui on Thursday urged his people to work hard and concentrate on "mind reform" in the Year of the Ox.

"On the eve of the new year, what needs to be cleaned up is not only our external environment and appearance, but also our mind," Lee said in his annual address on the eve of the Lunar New Year, which begins on Friday.

Lee praised the island's economic miracle, personal freedom and democracy, but said he was deeply concerned by the materialism that he said was eroding the social foundation and corrupting Taiwan people.
"As self-awareness grows, (the) individual's sense of social responsibility is declining, materialism and chaos in the society are blocking our progress," Lee said.
"A peaceful mind is the source of all happinesses and foundation of social stability."
Lee, whose speech was broadcast on state radio and could be heard in mainland China, did not specifically mention relations between Taipei and Beijing or other sensitive political issues.
China has regarded the Nationalist-ruled island as a rebel province since a civil war separated them in 1949.
"Together let us glorify the spirit of the ox," Lee said, urging people to work hard without complaints in the new year.
Last year was the Year of the Rat.
